column2: the writer's notes (doubts; where the article disagrees with the entry): for the data check

Entry says the Ghilzai revolt under Mir Wais began 1704; article says Mirwais revolted in 1709 killing Gurgin Khan. Revolt date left out of the text. Ahmad Shah Durrani's burial: article lists him buried in the city.
Entry says Čapek died soon after the Munich Agreement; article does not mention Munich by name, so omitted. Article gives Josef arrested in September (year unstated).

Article says Kublai was second son of Tolui with Sorghaghtani but also fourth son of Tolui overall; text says second son of Tolui and Sorghaghtani as in the lead. Article gives Java only as a listed invasion; nothing on Majapahit, so omitted.

Entry says the Yongli Emperor was executed at Kunming in 1662; article does not mention it, so omitted. Article says 'Founded in 765' for Tuodong and 'nearly 2,400-year history' (townships from 279 BCE); not printed.
Entry says the prefecture was formed after abolition of the domains in 1871 and covers Sagami and part of Musashi; article does not give the formation date, so omitted.

Entry says the Kingdom was established in 1815; article gives 1813 for the Sovereign Principality and no 1815 date, only a bicentennial 2013-2015. Left out the founding year of the Kingdom. Omitted current office holders.
Article's history section is thin (lead + 17th century, Jews, 1945). Entry's Thököly/Rákóczi risings and Rákóczi's 1906 reburial are not in the given text; left out.
Entry says Mongol destruction in 1240 and refounding by Muscovy in 1586; article says Batu devastated it in 1239 and a new fortress was built in 1596 (also 'by 1603'). Both dates left out.
Entry says capital of Imereti from the 13th century; article says from the 15th century. Start date left out. Entry gives Bagrati completed 1003; article says early 11th century.
Entry says islands were divided between Japan and Russia in 1855 and that the chain is about 1,200 km; article gives about 1,300 km and does not mention 1855 in the given text. Both left out.
Article gives Templars' fleet escape as conspiracy theory; omitted.
Entry's Maravi states, Ngoni and Yao rulers and Nyasaland protectorate are not in the given text; left out.
Entry says Kamakura and Koga kubo governed for the Ashikaga and the Later Hojo held it; not in the given text, left out.

Entry's Sasanian and Byzantine cavalry material is not in the given article text; left out. Article says first knights under Charlemagne while also saying institution is well established by 10th century.
Entry's Alemanni, Saint Gall and the bishopric of Constance are not in the given article text; left out.
Entry says Champlain reached its shores in 1615; not in the given text, left out.
Article says Nguni occupation from the early 1300s and the Zulu Kingdom in the 1830s-40s; entry calls the region the Zulu heartland. No conflict.
Entry gives Young's patent as 1850; article gives 1850 for the process and 1852 for the US patent, and Gesner's first patent as 1854.
Entry says Susa was chief city and sugar cane and textiles; not in the given text, left out. Omitted the 2026 section.

Entry says the Mongol conquest came in the 1230s-1240s; article says mid-13th century. Entry says Rus' helped destroy the Khazars in the 10th century; article gives Sviatoslav I's war of conquest (r. 943-972). Not printed.

Article says Fenton debuted the first melody in 1870 and also that the idea came in 1869; the 1870 date is left out. Left out: events after 2010 (Osaka teachers, 2011 Supreme Court rulings), details of protocol.
Article dates first bishop to c.585; entry says around 600: left out. Left out: 'largest diocese' (not in article), cross-border shopping, transport, notable people lists.

Article says the crown was offered in 1612; the entry says Michael Romanov's election in 1613: the election is not given a year here and 1613 is not printed. Article gives 1152 founding by Yury Dolgoruky (entry says 12th century, traditionally Yuri Dolgoruky): left out. Left out: Russian Revolution club, 1990 nuclear referendum, twin towns, 2022 items.
Article does not give the lake's length or area; entry's figures not repeated. Pannonia not mentioned in article (Roman name Pelso only). Left out: festivals, tourism events, town lists.

Article dates Kryuchkov chairmanship 1988-1991. Warsaw Pact invasion of 1968 is implied by 'Red Army's invasion' in article; the name 'Warsaw Pact' is not in the file - check flagged. Left out: US espionage sections, Bangladesh, Afghanistan details, chairmen list.
Article says the Italian Empire was established in 1882 and describes the kingdom's colonies loosely; left out. Mussolini 'dismissed' in 1944 per symbols section vs 1943 elsewhere: left out.
Left out: affairs, children, honours, music patronage.

Article gives founding in the 1680s and capital in 1695; entry gives no date; both left out. Article says British took over in 1896 and burned city in 1874; entry says occupied during wars. Left out: 2024 environmental report, as-of items, economy, sports.

Article is thin on history and says nothing of 1871, the Hosokawa or the Satsuma Rebellion; the entry's own statements are not repeated. Left out: economic plans (2023), sports, universities, transport lists, notable people.
Article calls Karlstad 20th-largest city in Sweden (ranking, left out). Left out: sports, economy figures, climate records, notable residents.

Article gives founding as Revive China Society 24 Nov 1894 in Honolulu, reformed under the current name in 1919; the entry says founded 1912 growing out of the Tongmenghui. No founding date printed. Article says 'sole ruling party 1928 to 1949'; entry 'ruled from Nanjing from 1928' - Nanjing not in article. Left out: current chair, elections after 2008, cross-strait stance, affiliated parties.

Article gives Khazar dominance c.650-965 and Atil's conquest by 969 by Sviatoslav; entry says decline after attacks by Kievan Rus' in the 10th century. No date for the fall printed. Left out: genetics, Khazar myth detail, literature, city lists.
Entry says ruled by Hohenzollern from 1701; article gives kingdom 1701-1918. Left out: Napoleonic War details, religious census figures, title dispute, plague.

Article says Greek colonists from Miletus founded Panticapaeum in the 7th century BCE; entry says around 600 BCE; founding date not printed. Left out: events after 2014, 2007 storm, 2018 shooting, bridge, economy, notable people.
Article states the kingdom lasted from 1707 to end of 1800 and was merged on 1 Jan 1801. Left out: etymology details, monarchs list, East India Company.

Entry says castle built early 17th century; article gives only 1588 daimyo appointment and 'afterwards' - date of building not printed. Left out: population figures, climate (contains a date of 2026 slip), mayor, working mother incident, transport, sports, sister cities.

Article's reign dates for Vima Kadphises and Kanishka are inconsistent (95-127 vs 113-127; Kanishka 127-150 vs 151), so no reign dates are printed beyond the c.30-c.375 span. Left out: coin deity list, rulers list.

Article says Arrapkha was under Mittani control in the 1450s; entry says capital of a Hurrian kingdom in the 15th and 14th centuries BCE - not repeated or contradicted. Oil at Baba Gurgur (entry, 1927) not in article. Left out: Arabization, 1991-2017 events, the status dispute, violence, notable people.

Entry says Dönitz 'became head of state on 1 May 1945'; article says named successor on 30 April and does not give 1 May: not printed. Article says the Nuremberg verdict was 'not guilty on count one, guilty on counts two and three' (printed as such). Left out: IQ test, decorations, Nazification details, intelligence analysis.
Article's Venice dates (east 1405, west 1426) consistent with entry's 'from the 15th century'. Left out: seismic history, tourism changes, transport, myths, Napoleonic and independence wars.

Founding year: the article says founded 1118 in its lead, but 1119 for the approach to Baldwin II; the entry says c. 1119. Founding year left out of the text. The article says in one place the order was disbanded in 1309 (Modern organizations) and elsewhere 1312; the entry says 1312. Used 1312. Cyprus purchase of 1191 is in the entry but not in the saved excerpt; not repeated. Left out: Chinon Parchment, popular culture and legends, the Temple district of London.

Entry says Daniel of Moscow seized Kolomna around 1301; article says only that it became the first town incorporated into the Moscow Principality in 1301. Left out: notable people, sports, twin towns, administrative detail.

Entry says MAT co-founded in 1898; article says meeting 4 July 1897 led to creation; text says meeting 1897 and Seagull 1898 without a founding year. Article says 'a son and two surviving daughters' is inferred from first daughter dying in infancy, second daughter Kira, son Igor. Left out: Cheka arrest 1918, Immenstadt episode, Meyerhold, Maeterlinck, Craig details.

Left out: 13th-century fight between Fernando of Portugal and Louis VIII (article's pairing looks doubtful); all modern leisure, sport, transport, notable people sections. Article gives 'battles called Battle of Courtrai' in 1302, 1382, 1580 etc.; not used.

Ottoman conquest: article says 1428 (and 'Germiyanids passed...' not dated); entry says 1429. Left the year out. Left out: Germiyanid capital claim (not in article), bishopric list, economy, twin towns, notable people. Third heading is The place today though it covers Ottoman ceramics.

Left out: genetics sections, Fuyu Kyrgyz detail, notable people, US organisations, Shia communities. Article lists residence in Uzbekistan, Pakistan; entry says Kyrgyzstan, China, Tajikistan, Afghanistan; not repeated. Article does not mention Manas epic; text mentions Manas only in the founding myth.

Article says the territory was divided and La Pampa became a province in 1945; entry says 1951. Year of provincehood left out. Article says territory erected in 1884 'containing the Río Negro Province' (odd); worded as 'territory that included'. Article does not date the conquest (entry: 1878-1879); left as 'the 19th century'. Left out: climate figures, economic figures, villages.
Left out: bathymetry details, ecological collapse and action plans (recent), emission control area, protected area lists. Article says 'Norwegian Sea' as archaic name; kept as given.

Article says Kermanshah became the Sasanian capital and was conquered by Arabs in 629; both look doubtful, left out. Article says 'founded the city in 390' while also attributing to Sasanians generally; used 'is said to have'. Left out: recent protests (2026), population figures, climate, universities, schools.

Article contradicts itself on dissolution: 'largely dissolved by the mid-1990s and surrendered completely in 1999'; text says 1994 amnesty and 1999. Left out: the article's 'black sheep' remark and economic characterisations of present Cambodia (present-day judgement), UN seat dispute, media and dialogue sections.

Entry says Stalin deported the whole Korean population of the Soviet Far East in 1937; article only says 'forcibly deported during Stalin regime'. Used article wording, no year. Left out: genetics, population figures, diaspora statistics, mixed-descent populations (modern/sensitive), economics of Korean Americans.

Article says bishopric secularised 1572 and Denmark from 1572; entry says 'passed to Denmark in 1559' (sale of lands). Text states the 1559 sale and the 1572 secularisation as the article does; no contradiction intended. Left out: neighbourhoods, population, event detail.

Article gives dates of sons' deaths and reign length; entry says 26th century BCE; no figures given. Left out: Westcar Papyrus detail, Manetho, Diodorus, Arabic traditions, family lists beyond the confirmed ones.

Entry says both passed to Bavaria 1802-1803 'and were merged into one town'; article says united 1819. Text gives both dates separately. Left out: transport, education, sport, notable people, twin towns, Dachau subcamps.

Entry mentions Nader Shah 1740; not in the article, so not repeated. Left out: industry, transport, education, sister cities, notable people, madrasah lists. Article gives both 'Muhammad Aminxon Madrasah' etc.; omitted.

Article says empire lasted 802 to 1431; entry says ninth to fifteenth century. Consistent. Article says Jayavarman II became king in 790 and also that his reign was 802–835; text avoids reign dates. Left out: Jayavarman VII (section empty in excerpt), relations with Java, military details, Angkor Thom walls.

Left out: Soviet-era ruling elite claim (not in article), 1996 protests and prison riot, water project, 2010 attack, 2017 detention, transport, education. Article says Khujand 'dating back about 2,500 years'; entry says Alexandria Eschate 329 BCE; consistent.

Entry says about 1,300 km, article says 1,400 km; length left out. Entry's Satavahanas, Ikshvakus, Eastern Chalukyas are not in the article and not repeated. Left out: floods (2009, 2024, 2025), pollution and water sharing disputes, mineral lists. Article is thin on history; history section is mostly pilgrimage and Jain reference.

Entry says Japanese occupation December 1941 to 1945; article says 1942 to 1945. Year range left out. Article offers two accounts of the name: Kuching in use before Brooke arrived, and also that it was Sarawak until Charles Brooke renamed it in 1872 (contradiction); paragraph mentions both -- consider removing the 1872 sentence. Entry mentions Astana palace and Fort Margherita; not in saved article text (fort mentioned generically).

Entry mentions Greek colonies and Bosporan Kingdom 6th century BCE / c. 480 BCE; not in the saved article, so not repeated. Left out: 2003 dispute, storms, 2018 incident, wars since 2014, 2022-2024 events and oil spills (recent). Bridge entries after 2010 limited to the bare facts of opening.

Article says Lotf Ali Khan captured Kerman in 1794 and was then besieged six months by Agha Muhammad; entry says Lotf Ali was captured there after a siege. Left the chronology and the siege out. Article's eyeball detail stated flatly there.
Article says renamed 1967; entry says 1968: rename year left out. Article's later sections (mayors, WiFi etc.) skipped as current affairs.

Skipped: wealth and yacht figures, WikiLeaks cable, Panama Papers, Seychelles land dealings, 2022 Israel normalisation (recent/contested). Dates of re-election and 2005 council reform as article gives.

Entry says typhoons destroyed 'Yuan' fleets; article says Mongol-Koryo fleets under Kublai Khan, 1274 and 1281 (entry gives 'late thirteenth century'); no conflict. Article is mostly about the WWII units; the 13th-century storms get one sentence there, so the text covers the term and its WWII use.
Article says King Mu reigned 976-922 BCE; left out.
Article calls founder Charles II; entry says Archduke Charles of Austria; consistent. Skipped modern industry and settlement lists.

Article does not mention Normans, Italian counts palatine or British protection (in entry); not repeated. Article's 1953 earthquake section has no description; only olive-press detail used. Article says Ottoman rule 'lasted only until 1500' with no start.
SKIPPED: article has under about 250 words of substance and mostly repeats the description (airport, Cold War base, closure 2006)
Article: died Medina or Homs 642 (consistent with entry). Contested dates (Fahl 634/635; Damascus siege, Umar's demotion timing) left loose. Muhajir/Siffin and later kin omitted.
Article's Baldwin II, Fulk, Third Crusade sections not in excerpt; text relies on the lead and shown sections.

Entry says bishops of Cammin made it a main residence; article says bishops moved residence to Kołobrzeg in 1276 and administered the diocese from Koszalin. Text says only the latter (it states what the article states).
Entry says fell to Baybars 1271; article lead names only the Mamluk Sultanate. Skipped civil-war damage.

Article says Ali's capital 'final capital of his caliphate'; entry says capital of Ali; consistent. Article's Kufic script origin is partly disputed in the text (angular script a century older than the town); I said derived from the script of al-Hirah as article says.
Article says 'original song two stanzas', same as entry. Skipped recording soloists. Entry says anthem of Czech Republic from 1993; article says kept after December 1992 split; no conflict.
Article says 'Until 1735 ruled by Austria'; Charles winning at Bitonto in 1734. Entry says Ferdinand I merged 1816: consistent.
Article says Kingston was named capital on 10 February 1841; entry says capital 1841-44; consistent. Skipped industry/sports and recent bridge failure.
Article says Russia captured Kokand in 1883 under Skobelev; entry says Russia annexed Kokand in 1876. Year left out. Spelling Schulyer as the article prints it.

Article says the Dutch took fort 1653 (entry says VOC took the fort there in 1653; article says built Fort Concordia in 1653). Wording uses 'built' per article; entry says 'took'. Possible disagreement, noted; avoided saying 'took'. Entry says Lifau; article does not mention Lifau.

Article says UNIP-only rule followed violence in 1968 and the constitution was promulgated 1973; entry says one-party state 1972. Year of the one-party state left out of the text (article's 1973 constitution vs entry's 1972). Article's judgements ('dictator', 'ineptness', fascism comparison) left out.

Article sentence about Khwarazmian dynasty founding date is 'debatable'; text gives Anushtegin 1077 as the article does. Entry says empire 12th-early 13th c.; consistent. Article typo 'Second Persian invasion ... t80 BCE' not used.

Article: Leopold had the castle and collegiate church built in 1114 and transferred it to Augustinian canons in 1133; entry says he founded the Augustinian abbey in 1114. Text avoids saying who founded the abbey when. Entry says 'briefly a residence'; article says 1113 residence, also Leopold VI. Article dates Verdun Altar only '12th century' (entry 1181): not stated.
Entry: royal mint 'around 1300'; article: 'shortly after 1300'. Wrote 'shortly afterwards'. Left out tourism figures and 2026 monument protection.

Entry says Habsburg rule from the sixteenth century; article: Habsburgs held throne from 1526 to 1918 (consistent). Trianon territorial loss given as 72% in lead, other figures later; omitted all figures.
Article's speaker countries include Gabon; entry omits it. Article says Gomes's catechism does not survive.
Entry says Koine spread after Alexander's conquests; article says it arose within his armies and dates post-classical Greek from 323 BCE. Left Seleucid administration claim to entry.

Entry says the Sikh Empire 'extended its control towards the pass'; article says Ranjit Singh's Sikhs captured it in 1837. Left as article states; not a hard conflict. Omitted post-2001 events and cultural references.

Entry names the Barroso II blowout of 1922 at Cabimas; article does not mention it, only large-scale exploitation from 1922 (consistent). Omitted pollution, population figures and lightning statistics.

Article has thin substance (~270 words of usable material). Entry dates temples c. 950-1050; article only says many were built in Dhanga's reign (c. 950-1002): left it so. Rediscovery date 1819 per article.

Article gives atabegs ruling 1184-1596 and Abbas ending the line in 1006 AH (1597-98): kept both as in article. Entry: 'late 12th century' consistent. Article's Sasanian foundation claims are hedged (Shapur I or II).

Entry: 1469 marriage laid foundation; article: crowns united 1479 (the entry doesn't say 1479), both given. Article's 1391 figures (100,000 converted etc.) omitted as uncertain. Article's Alhambra Decree/Inquisition left out.

Entry names the Second Congo War 1999-2000 battle and Simba rebellion; article mentions the 1964 siege and the 1990s but not the 1999-2000 fighting, so those are left to the entry. Omitted population estimates, economy rankings, culture details.
Article gives first palace destroyed c. 1700 BCE, partial destruction c. 1450, fire c. 1350, consistent with entry. 'Colonia Iulia Nobilis Cnossus' from article.
Article: Kautsky lived in London 1885-1888 and 1889-1890, stated broadly as 1885-1890. Born/died dates in desc: 1854-1938, consistent.
Article has nothing on Byzantine, Chobanid, Candarid or Ottoman annexation history, which the entry covers. Material is thin. Date of Ibn Battuta visit not given in article, so left undated.

Article contradicts itself on 822/824/825 for the church and era; the text gives only 825, as the entry does. Article says Marco Polo visited c. 1275 'in Chinese service'. Omitted rankings (EIU growth), census figures, mayor.

Entry says thousands of French and German settlers died; article says 10,000-12,000 mostly Frenchmen, about 6,000 died, no Germans mentioned: text avoids 'German'. Entry says first launch 1968: not in article. Omitted crime, demographics.

Entry says annexed by Britain 1888, joined Gilbert and Ellice Islands colony 1919, Cook sighted it on Christmas Eve 1777: none in article; avoided. Article says tests 'late 1950s'. Omitted climate-change speculation, tourism, cables.
Article material is thin. Left out population density figures and rankings. Entry says 'one of the most densely populated places in the world': not repeated.

Entry: Qasim son of Ulugh Muhammad; article gives Ulugh Muhammad as Khan of Kazan who received the lands in 1445 and says Qasim fled with brother Yosif after losing a bid against brother Mäxmüd (so a brother of Mahmud; parentage not stated). Text avoids saying son. Article's 'Oluğ Möxämmäd' rendered Ulugh Muhammad as in entry. Thin article (~330 words used).

Entry says Chechen fighters took hundreds of hostages in 1996; article says only the airbase raid and 78 soldiers killed: text follows the article. Article's 'Germans briefly took Kizlyar' in 1942 kept. Omitted 2018 shooting, demographics. Article thin (~260 words).

Article gives Polish-French siege wording only in lead; body says Grande Armée plus Polish insurgents. The entry says 1248 belonged to the bishops; article says 1248 exchange of lands and 1276 sovereignty over the town: not printed 1248, no conflict. Article says Kołobrzeg is 'capital of Kołobrzeg County'. Omitted Nazi-era persecution and forced labour, the Goebbels film, sister cities.

Article gives death as c. 2532 BC and a reign 2558-2532 BC 'some authors'; not printed (entry only says 26th century BCE). Article says Sphinx attribution 'according to some Egyptologists, unconfirmed'; text states the grounds without the hedge word. Entry's diorite statue not mentioned in article. Reign section has four paragraphs; no Death and legacy section as death is not told.

Article's Edo passage says 'His son, Yoshiyasu was transferred ... 1724' (garbled: probably Yoshisato); I wrote that the domain passed to Yamato-Koriyama in 1724 without naming who. Article says 1907 flood killed 233 (apparently in the prefecture); I attributed it to the prefecture. Article's population figure dated 2019: rounded to about 188,000. Entry says 'under direct shogunate rule for much of the time': consistent.

Article says both 'founded during the late 19th century' and 'established by Sultan Muhammad II in 1844'; the entry says 19th century. Printed 1844 (inside the entry's 19th century) and did not say 'late'. Article's 'Royal Palace ... before' sentence is garbled; kept to a bare statement. Omitted religion percentages, transport, shopping.

Article says the Primary Chronicle gives 1051 or 1074 as founding date: not printed (entry says 1051). Article does not name Theodosius. Article gives two dates for the Soviet museum (1926 and 1928): left out. Omitted all events since 2022, jurisdiction disputes and the 2026 attacks.

Article gives 'dating as far back as 641' for oral materials; omitted. Preface-based account is hedged. Entry says 'founding text of Shinto'; article says myths inspired Shinto orthodoxy and practices; I kept to the practices wording.

Article calls the principality 'Arbër' in one place and 'Arbanon' in the lead; used the entry's Arbanon. Article's siege counts are inconsistent (lead: three sieges until 1468 then a fourth in 1478; body: four times 1450-1477 then conquered 1478); I listed dated sieges without counts. Skanderbeg's governorship (1437-38) and the 1476 siege omitted.

Article says Lazar's ruling years 1371-1389 and that the tower of Milica is a fragment; the crow legend is hedged 'according to legend'. The 1944 liberation: article says '14 October' without year; placed after 1943 events as the article does and wrote 1944, which is implied (Autumn 1944 elsewhere). Omitted post-2002 industrial decline, unemployment rate, and communist purge figures.

Article makes strong claims on 'ethnocide', colonization and demographic loss (partly UNPO wording, partisan): left out except the deportation of 1944, which the article says the Russian government does not acknowledge (not printed). Article says the Caucasian War ended 30 December 1869 yet the Shamkhalate was abolished in 1867; I give 1867 only. Article's Kipchak migration-wave narrative (Timur vs Tokhtamysh) is loosely worded; omitted.
Entry's mention of Gupta coins is not in the article (article: Yaudheya and Kushan coins; six-head type post-Gupta); not repeated. Ramayana and Mahabharata dates omitted.

Article gives the Arab conquest as 647 CE in one place and c. 651 in another: printed 'in the middle of the 7th century'. Mongol phrase is quoted in the article without a name, attributed to 'one historian'. Iran's Khorasan Province (1906-2004) omitted.

Article gives 'Eternal Peace of 532' and 'Perpetual Peace'; used the lead's term. Article says a fifty-year peace in 562 and also '51 year peace treaty' later; printed 'fifty-year'. Peace of 531 vs 532 inconsistency in the article ('peace agreement ... in 531'); printed 532 as lead. Entry's 'greatest rulers' consistent.
Article spells William Marshall; the entry writes Marshal. Kilkenny College (1538) omitted. 'Thirteenth-largest' omitted per rule.

Article's lead says 'kings of Aragon (1054-1134)' while the body says García Sánchez III reigned 1035-1054: dates of Aragonese rule not printed. Sancho the Great's dates not given in the article. Article says 'Ferdinand II of Aragon ... 1512 (permanently annexed 1524)'; printed 1512 and 1515. Entry's Las Navas de Tolosa claim is not in the article; not repeated.
Article says Alexandra's crown 1901 (lead) and coronation 1902: dates omitted. Entry says 'Afghan and Sikh hands': consistent. Omitted recent claims and politicians' quotations.
Omitted labour-day minimums and penalties, Belarus and statistics tables.

Article's lead says he led the first government in '1919 and 1920'; body says Chancellor 1918-1920 and the entry says 1918-1920: used 1918-1920. The Feingold statement is one account (the article's 'Antisemitism' section asserts it in its own voice): attributed.

Article says Italians occupied 12 May 1912, then Treaty of Lausanne 1923 'joined ... Italian Aegean Islands'; I wrote 'confirmed'. Article does not use 'Hellenistic'; the entry's rule of Rhodes in the Hellenistic period is not repeated. Omitted beaches, transport, climate. Saria earthquake detail omitted.

Article does not mention the Treaty of Stolbovo, 1617, Peter the Great's capture in 1710 or the Treaty of Nystad (all in the entry); not contradicted. Omitted most of the 20th-century population figures.

Article says Komotini was handed to Greece in 1919 by the Treaty of Neuilly and 'liberated' in May 1920; the entry says Greece in 1920: printed 'after the First World War'. The legend of Parrasios' daughter omitted.
Article says Leopold died 1728 and funeral services 1729 (as given); desc gives 1603-1847 residence, consistent. Left out homeopathy 'world capital' claim and 2013 society move.
Left out Jayaswal's democracy argument and modern jajmani remark.
Left out fertility (article stresses she was not a mother goddess; desc says fertility, so not contradicted or repeated). Left out Hislop/Easter, rape myth, details.
Left out causes theories (regime type etc.), Crimea 2014 and other recent cases. Desc mentions interwar successor states; article does not, not repeated.
Article gives landing as 4 October in one place and 10 October in another; left out. Casualty/reprisal figures omitted as inconsistent.
Birth date 10 or 11 January 1815 in article; left out. Left out rankings/polls and the 2015 commission.
Article says 'at least 4,000 years old' (as desc). Left out 1982, 1992 military uses and design detail.
Article: reign 590-628 with one-year interruption; desc r. 590-628. Left out Bahram's later fate details and Islamic tradition letter.
Desc mentions Idah as Igala capital; article does not, left out. Left out floods, officeholders, population estimates, rankings. Flora Shaw claim attributed ('account given').

CONFLICT: desc says Stephen of Perm converted many Komi in the late 14th century; article says Great Perm remained unconverted for another century and the duke was baptised only in 1470. I printed neither the conversion claim nor the 1470 baptism. Left out genetics, census figures, notable people.

Article does not date the 1848 Reichstag as Nov 1848-Mar 1849 or call it 'Reichstag' (it says Constitutive Imperial Congress); desc dates not repeated. Left out notable people, film locations, sports.

Desc says Ilorin Emirate founded in 1820s; article dates the jihad's annexation to mid-1800s and does not mention the emirate. Left out the jihad date and emirate. Left out politics, incidents, 2023-2026 items, population figures.

Article says last vestiges of Roman rule ended 472 (consistent with Visigoth taking of Tarragona), desc says fell to Germanic peoples in 5th century. Article gives inconsistent province-division dates (197 BCE, 1st c. BCE, 27 BCE); I used 27 BCE only. Left out prehistory and climate.

Article says he is considered second king by most Egyptologists, with Narmer=Menes generally accepted, while others identify Aha with Menes; desc says 'often identified with Menes' and 'tradition credits founding of Memphis': I left out the Menes question and attribute only Manetho's palace remark. Dates: article fl. c. 3085 BC / 31st century BC; desc 'around 3100 BCE'; no date printed. Left out Levant trade detail, Manetho's physician claim, family tomb candidates.
Desc says assembly of 788 condemned Tassilo III; article does not mention it, left out. Article gives both 'died in Ingelheim' and 'summer tent on island off Ingelheim'; I used both as one account.

Desc says marriage 1386; article: Union of Krewo 1385, baptism 1386, marriage date not given; left out marriage year. Union of Lublin 1569 not in my text (desc has it). Left out genetics. 'Marriages' in 1515 sentence: article says Louis II married Mary of Austria, Anne to Ferdinand.
Article: Flodden 9 September; 'body found the following day' (as I wrote). Left out judgement 'most successful Stewart monarch', finances detail, fiction.
Desc says first permanent English colony in North America; article says Americas.

Desc gives Colloquium heptaplomeres as 1588 and 'seven men'; article gives no date and only 'towards the end of his life'; I omitted the date. Article says wrote Six Books in 1576 (desc: 1576). Left out reception by country and Frankish Gauls theory.

Desc says Garun Gabas, associated with kingdom of Biram, and emirates Hadejia and Gumel; article places Biram at Hadejia and does not mention Garun Gabas or Gumel as emirate. I left out Garun Gabas. Left out floods, poverty and demographic statistics.

Article calls Philip IV of Spain 'Philip III' of Portugal; used as given. Crux fidelis attribution (19th-century) left out. Article says Spanish recognition in 1668 'in a subsequent reign'; desc says same.
Doubtful: article says Anchieta helped executioner of Jacques le Balleur 'much disputed' - left out. Article's 'Tapuia Indians' left out. 1563 captivity from tradition.
Article says Chalcedon 'came into Ottoman hands in 1353'; desc silent. Omitted political and index claims. Article says conquest 'a full century before Constantinople'.
Third heading reused for religion and heritage; silk weaving and politics left out.

Article inconsistent on Oyo tribute dates (1728-1740 warfare; since 1748; 1732-1823); tribute dates omitted. Entry says freed from Oyo; article says Ghezo sought to remove Oyo yoke after 1818. Left Ghezo wording vague.
Article's medieval, early modern and modern history sections are empty; written from the lead and origins. Alexander III bull 1179.
